texts.preamble: Deepak Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 April, 2025 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: G. S. Ahluwalia Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:7701 1 M.Cr.C. In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At G Wa L I O R Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia On The 2nd Of April, 2025 Misc. Criminal Case No. 52964 of 2023 Deepak Rai And Others Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others Appearance: Shri Rahul Yadav - Advocate for applicants. Dr. Anjali Gyanani - Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1/Stat Shri Akhilesh Dubey- Advocate for respondent No.2. Order
texts.facts: This application, under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR in Crime No.33/2023 registered at Mahila Police Station Vidisha for offences under Sections 498A, 294, 323, 506 and 34 of IPC. 2. Applicant No.1 is husband, applicant No.2 is father-in-law and applicant No.3 is mother-in-law of respondent No.2. 3. According to prosecution case, respondent No.2 lodged an FIR on 28.10.2023 alleging therein that she got married to applicant No.1 on 03.05.2022 in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals. Her father had spent a total amount of Rs.12 lacs in marriage. A cash amount of Rs.Seven Lacs was given apart from ornaments as well as household articles. Respondent No.2 had stayed in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7701 matrimonial house for fifteen months. During these fifteen months, she was harassed and treated with cruelty by applicants on the ground of further demand of Rs.Seven Lacs. Since respondent No.2 was not in a position to fulfill the demand, therefore, she was beaten regularly and she was forced to face the situation of starvation. Mobile of respondent No.2 was also snatched away with a solitary intention that she may not inform the act of Deepak Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139881784/ 1 cruelty to her parents. It was further alleged that father of respondent No.2 is an ordinary employee in Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti, Vidisha and he is not in a position to fulfill the additional demand of Rs.Seven Lacs. On 01.12.2022, respondent No.2 was badly beaten by her husband and boiling water was thrown on respondent No.2 as a result she was in severe pain. Respondent No.2 was not taken to the hospital but local treatment was got done in the house itself. Again on 15.04.2023, respondent No.2 was beaten by her husband. Although respondent No.2 tried to contact Dial 100 but the phone was not picked up by the Police. Again on 06.07.2023, respondent No.2 was badly beaten and ultimately, on 09.07.2023 respondent No.2 came back to her parental home along with her parents. On account of severe beating given by her husband, she had sustained injuries on her neck. It was alleged that on account of non-fulfillment of demand of Rs.Seven Lacs, respondent No.2 has been ousted from her matrimonial house by applicant No.1 and respondent No.2 is residing with her parents from 11.07.2023. Later on, applicant No.1 went to parental home of respondent No.2 on multiple occasions and also abused her filthily, threatened to kill her and raised demand of Rs.Seven Lacs. 4. Challenging the FIR lodged by respondent No.2, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that FIR in question was lodged by way of counterblast to the application filed by applicant No.1, under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act. It is further submitted that even if the entire FIR is read, then it is clear that major allegations are against applicant No.1. It is further submitted that respondent No.2 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7701 had already suffered burn injuries much prior to her marriage and the allegation of throwing boiling water by applicant No.1 is false. 5. Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State as well as complainant. By referring to the case diary, it is submitted by counsel for State that in her statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., respondent No.2 has levelled serious allegations against applicants No.2 and 3 also. Respondent No.2 in her statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. has specifically stated that she stayed in her matrimonial house for 15 months properly and thereafter applicants started harassing and treating her with cruelty on account of less dowry. Whenever she replied that her parents are not in a position to fulfill their additional demands, then applicant No.1 and applicant No.3 used to behave cruelly and both used to beat her. Applicant No.3 was insisting that food should not be given to respondent No.2. She also insisted that applicant No.1 should not talk to respondent No.2 and they were also not giving her household expenses. Whenever applicants including applicants No.2 and 3 used to come to her parental home to take her back then they were constantly demanding dowry. Whenever respondent No.2 informed about maltreatment by her husband and mother-in-law to applicant No.2, then applicant No.2 used to take the side of applicants No.1 and 3. It was further alleged that applicant No.3 along with applicant No.1 used to abuse her filthily in the name of mother and sister and they were also extending threat that in case if incident is narrated to anybody, then she would be killed. Thus, there are specific allegations of demand of dowry and cruelty against applicant No.3. So far as applicant No.2 is concerned, there is specific allegation that after fifteen months of marriage, applicant No.2 also started making demand of dowry and treated Deepak Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139881784/ 2 her with cruelty.
texts.arguments: 8. Supreme Court in the case of Taramani Parakh Vs. State of Madhya NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7701 Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 11 SCC 260 has held as under:- "12. In Kailash Chandra Agrawal v. State of U.P. (2014) 16 SCC 551, it was observed (SCC p. 553, paras 8-9): "8. In Kans Raj v. State of Punjab (2000) 5 SCC 207 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 935 : (2000) 3 SCR 662] it was observed (SCC p. 217, para 5): "5. ... A tendency has, however, developed for roping in all relations of the in-laws of the deceased wives in the matters of dowry deaths which, if not discouraged, is likely to affect the case of the prosecution even against the real culprits. In their overenthusiasm and anxiety to seek conviction for maximum people, the parents of the deceased have been found to be making efforts for involving other relations which ultimately weaken the case of the prosecution even against the real accused as appears to have happened in the instant case." Reference may be made to K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar, (2000) 8 SCC 547 : 2001 SCC (Cri) 27, Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Judicial Magistrate, (1998) 5 SCC 749 : 1998 SCC (Cri) 1400, State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 : NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7701 1992 SCC (Cri) 426 : AIR 1992 SC 604 and Asmathunnisa v. State of A.P., (2011) 11 SCC 259 : (2011) 3 SCC (Cri) 159." 13.
